name: Multiple Metaphyseal Dysplasia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Multiple Metaphyseal Dysplasia

criteria.description: Irregular, flared, and widened metaphyses on radiographs
Short stature with disproportionate shortening of the limbs
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes such as MATN3, COL9A1, COL9A2, or COL9A3
Joint pain and stiffness, especially in knees and ankles

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic metaphyseal radiographic abnormalities plus clinical features consistent with metaphyseal dysplasia; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical and radiographic; genetic testing aids confirmation and subtype classification.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Metaphyseal irregularities with flaring and cupping
Disproportionate short stature with limb shortening
searchTerms: short height with short arms and legs

common.symptomName: Gait abnormalities due to limb deformities
searchTerms: abnormal gait due to limb shape
difficulty walking caused by limb issues

common.symptomName: Mild genu valgum or varum deformities
searchTerms: slight inward or outward knee bending

occasional.symptomName: Hip joint involvement with limited range of motion
searchTerms: hip joint pain and limited movement

rare.symptomName: Epiphyseal involvement leading to joint deformities
searchTerms: joint deformities from bone end problems
abnormal growth plate causing joint shape changes
epiphyseal damage leading to joint issues

laboratory: Normal routine laboratory tests; no specific biochemical markers
imaging: Radiographs showing metaphyseal irregularities, flaring, and cupping
genetic: Pathogenic variants in MATN3, COL9A1, COL9A2, or COL9A3 genes
other: Clinical assessment of growth parameters and joint function

distinguishingFeatures: Rhizomelic limb shortening rather than metaphyseal abnormalities
Involvement of spine and epiphyses more prominent

redFlags: Progressive joint deformities leading to severe functional impairment
Failure to thrive or disproportionate growth delay
references: Superti-Furga A, Unger S. Multiple metaphyseal dysplasia. In: GeneReviews® [Internet]. University of Washington, Seattle; 2020.
Orphanet: Multiple metaphyseal dysplasia. Orphanet Report Series; 2023.
